proposals.before: Not even Fan Kuai and Guan Ying of Han, nor Xu Dian of Wei, could outdo them.
proposals.after: Not even Fan Kuai and Guan Ying of Han, nor Xu Chu and Dian Wei of Wei, could outdo them.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許典 conventionally abbreviates Xu Chu (許褚) and Dian Wei (典韋), parallel to 樊灌 for Fan Kuai and Guan Ying; rendering as a single 'Xu Dian' is incorrect.

proposals.before: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Prince of Pingping, granted the lacquered coffin fittings of state, borne in the imperial hearse, with guards of the palace hall as his escort.
proposals.after: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Prince of Jianping, granted the lacquered coffin fittings of state, borne in the imperial hearse, with guards of the palace hall as his escort.
proposals.reason: 建平王 is Prince of Jianping; 'Pingping' is a mistranslation of the place-name Jianping.

proposals.before: His grandfather Bing rose to the post of Grand Provisioner.
proposals.after: His grandfather and father both rose to high office.
proposals.reason: 祖父並至大官 means grandfather and father both reached high office; 並 is the adverb 'both', not a personal name Bing, and 大官 is not specifically Grand Provisioner.

proposals.before: His grandfather Bing reached Grand Provisioner.
proposals.after: His grandfather and father both reached great office.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 並 is 'both', not the name Bing; 大官 is high office generally.

proposals.before: Jian was promoted to Grand Minister of Education and General Who Campaigns West, and raised to Duke of Wei commandery.
proposals.after: Jian was promoted to Grand Minister of Education and General Who Campaigns West, and raised to Prince of Wei commandery.
proposals.reason: 魏郡王 is a princely title (王), not a dukedom; 'Duke of Wei commandery' understates the rank.

proposals.before: During Emperor Xiaoming's reign he entered service as registrar in the granary bureau of the Ministry of Education.
proposals.after: During Emperor Shizong's reign he entered service as registrar in the granary bureau of the Ministry of Education.
proposals.reason: 世宗 is Emperor Xuanwu (temple name Shizong), not Emperor Xiaoming (Suzong); the English misidentifies the emperor.

proposals.before: He was buried at Guo Mountain, where a stele and ceremonial gate towers were erected for him.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous name Xiao.
proposals.reason: English text is shifted onto the following sentence; ZH 贈襄城王，諡曰孝 does not mention burial at Guo Mountain.

proposals.before: He was buried at Guo Mountain, and a stele and gateway towers were built for him.
proposals.after: Posthumously granted Prince of Xiangcheng; posthumous name Xiao.
proposals.reason: Literal English is misaligned with the Chinese of this unit.

proposals.before: Since the founding of Wei, no honored minister had received favor comparable to his.
proposals.after: He was buried at Guo Mountain, where a stele and ceremonial gate towers were erected for him.
proposals.reason: English belongs to this unit's Chinese 葬於崞山，為建碑闕, but the packet currently has the following sentence's English.

proposals.before: Since the rise of Wei, among honored ministers, none had favor and privilege comparable to his.
proposals.after: Buried at Guo Mountain, and a stele and gateway towers were built for him.
proposals.reason: Literal English is misaligned with this unit's Chinese.

proposals.before: His son Tong succeeded to the title.
proposals.after: Since the founding of Wei, no honored minister had received favor comparable to his.
proposals.reason: English is shifted from the next unit; this unit's Chinese is 自魏興，貴臣恩寵，無與為比.

proposals.before: His son Tong inherited the title.
proposals.after: Since the rise of Wei, among honored ministers, none had favor and privilege comparable to his.
proposals.reason: Literal English is misaligned with this unit's Chinese.

decisions.reason: s0020 pairs 漢之樊灌 with 魏之許典; 樊灌 is the fused abbreviation of Fan Kuai and Guan Ying, so 許典 likewise fuses Xu Chu (許褚) and Dian Wei (典韋). Rendering 許典 as a single person 'Xu Dian' is wrong; expanding to Xu Chu and Dian Wei restores the parallel.
s0025 has 建平王; 建平 is Jianping, not Pingping. The proposed replacement corrects only that fief name.
祖父並至大官 means his grandfather and father both reached high office: 並 is the adverb 'both', not a personal name Bing, and 大官 is general high office, not Grand Provisioner.
The literal repeats the same misreading of 並 as Bing and of 大官 as Grand Provisioner; 'grandfather and father both reached great office' matches the Chinese.
進爵魏郡王 advances him to prince (王) of Wei commandery; 'Duke' understates 王. The proposal changes only that rank label.
s0143 begins 世宗時; Northern Wei 世宗 is temple name Shizong (Xuanwu), not Xiaoming (肅宗). The literal already has Shizong; the idiomatic must match.
s0184 is 贈襄城王，諡曰孝; burial at 崞山 belongs to s0185. The current idiomatic is shifted one sentence forward; the proposal restores the posthumous title and name.
The literal of s0184 likewise carries s0185's burial wording; aligning it to the posthumous grant and 諡曰孝 corrects the misalignment.
s0185 is 葬於崞山，為建碑闕; the packet's idiomatic belongs to s0186. Restoring the burial-and-stele English matches this unit's Chinese.
The literal of s0185 is likewise shifted to s0186's favor comparison; the proposed burial wording matches 葬於崞山，為建碑闕.
s0186 is 自魏興，貴臣恩寵，無與為比; 'His son Tong succeeded' belongs to s0187. The proposal restores the correct English for this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自魏興，貴臣恩寵，無與為比

decisions.reason: The literal of s0186 is the same forward shift onto the succession sentence; restoring the Wei-founding favor comparison matches the Chinese.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0006 shows the title Emperor Xiaoming was created only by the bad idiomatic of 世宗時; s0143 supports Shizong, not Xiaoming.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English Xu Dian came only from reading 許典 as one person; the fused Chinese abbreviation remains valid, matching the 樊灌 claims that carry zh only.
Accepted r0001 likewise shows en Xu Dian for Dian Wei was an artifact of the single-person misreading; keep zh 許典 as the source abbreviation without that English form.
